scenes.title: The die broken on the Larkfield anvil

beats.speaker: shopkeeper
beats.text: Weights and measures, Larkfield! Here's the die that struck the light pennies, out of a dead working on the Kestrel. The Market Board has seen it. Now so will you.

beats.speaker: striker
beats.text: One blow on our own anvil, and it's done. Short weight, short life.

beats.speaker: shopkeeper
beats.text: Full weight in every till from today. Good trade to you all, and count your change anyway.

triggers.note: Light coin goes round (world text clipping); the striker's weighing is laid.

effect.reply: Short-weighed, every third one. Rims shaved and stamped again. Somebody with a jeweler's file and a good die. That's not Larkfield work. We'd have heard the hammer.

triggers.note: The warden showed the beam: the shopkeeper's two choices are laid (J1 later: per wolf).

effect.words: That beam is false. The Market Board should see it.
effect.reply: #oath#. Then tell the warden so to his face, and I'll write it on the wall behind the counter so I never forget the look of it.

effect.words: Leave it with me. I'll deal with the Counting House.
effect.reply: You? With them? Well. Mind they don't weigh you on it.

effect.words: Where does the jeweler go when she shuts the shop?
effect.reply: Out to the old Kestrel workings, with a basket and a lamp. Says she buys silver off the tailings. There's no silver in dead tailings. I've told her so. She cries at night about the factor's chalk on our door.

phases.journal: Larkfield's grain comes home short-weighed and paid in light coin. The shopkeeper at Larkfield Stores wants to know who is light.

effects.text: Fair price to you, and full weight, if you've got it. Count your change twice this week.

phases.journal: The coiners' dies are out of the Kestrel workings. What is to be done with an old jeweler who shaves the realm's coin?

effects.text: The dies are out of the Kestrel. Now, what's to be done with an old jeweler who shaves the realm's coin? That's the hard weighing.

effects.text: Good trade. Full-weight pennies in the till again, and the die broke on our own anvil.

phases.journal: Somebody paid an old jeweler's debt and broke her dies quietly. The light coin is gone.

effects.text: The light coin's gone, and nobody in the stocks for it. Weights and measures. I'll call that a fair price.

phases.journal: The jeweler still clips, and somebody takes a share. There is light coin about.

effects.text: Still light. Count your change twice, customer. Somebody's getting fat on our shavings, and Larkfield will find out who.

quests.title: Short-Weighed
quests.summary: Larkfield's grain is short-weighed at the Market Hall and paid in light coin. Find out who is light.

offer.say: #greet#, #address#. Slow and light. We send full wagons of Longmead sacks to the city, and the Market Hall pays for two-thirds, in coin with the rim shaved off besides. Ask the carter, watch the Hall's beam, and take their pennies to the striker at the anvil.
offer.accept: Carter, beam and anvil. I'll find the light one.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. A Counting House beam and a jeweler's file, both. Scales and silver, a city wolf shaving the realm's coin. Follow it to the Commons, customer. I'll keep my till shut till you're back.
